lines.text: Can brake fluid really free a rusted bolt better than the stuff that's made for it?
So he rusts 28 bolts on purpose and drips ten drops of each fluid on them.
The trick is capillary action which pulls a thin liquid into tiny gaps like a paper towel drinking a spill.
beats: ai:macro of thin golden oil creeping up into the tiny gaps of rusty bolt threads
ai:macro of tiny gaps between rusty steel threads filling with shiny oil
ai:a white paper towel soaking up a spilled blue drink on a table

lines.text: The brake fluid just sits on the washer like it gave up.
But a clear plastic block shows it still crawled all the way down the threads.
Fluid Film is so thick it just slimes the outside and never squeezes into the threads.
beats: ai:thick honey sitting on top of a narrow crack in rusty metal and not going in

lines.text: Seafoam breaks one loose at 104 foot pounds while a dry bolt needs 133.
Then viewers beg him to mix them all into one super oil which is risky because chemicals can react.
beats: ai:two chemicals reacting with white smoke in a glass beaker

lines.text: And the mix never crept down so a nut that was only hand tight needed 56 foot pounds.
The winner is Seafoam Deep Creep with CRC Knock'er Loose right behind it.
Because in rusty threads the gaps are microscopic so only the thinnest fluid gets in.
beats: ai:extreme close up of a rusty steel bolt thread showing tiny cracks and gaps between the threads

lines.text: So would you trust brake fluid on your next rusted bolt?
